- `@unknown default`: Compiler emits a warning, alerting us to update the code

body:
This PR implements a comprehensive package for handling WebSocket message responses in Flutter instant messaging applications. The package provides type-safe models with JSON serialization support for 37 different message types.

## What's New

### Core Models (16 classes)
Implemented 16 distinct model classes using `@JsonSerializable` annotations:

- **Authentication & Connection**: `LoginQrCodeData`, `LoginSuccessData`, `TokenExpiredData`, `InvalidUserData`, `NoInternetData`
- **Messaging**: `ReceiveMessageData`, `MsgMarkItemData`, `MsgRecallData`
- **User Status**: `OnlineOfflineData`
- **Room Management**: `RoomInfoChangeData`, `MyRoomInfoChangeData`, `RoomDissolutionData`, `MemberChangeData`
- **Friend Management**: `RequestApprovalFriendData`, `NewApplyData`
- **Base Model**: `EmptyData` for 21 message types with no payload

Each model includes:
- Required and optional fields with proper Dart types
- Automatic `fromJson()` and `toJson()` methods via code generation
- Null-safe implementation

### Infrastructure

**SocketEnvelope**: Message wrapper that parses WebSocket messages and automatically decodes them into typed models.

**MessageFactory**: Factory pattern with automatic registration for all 37 message types:
- Authentication: `loginQrCode`, `waitingAuthorize`, `loginSuccess`, `tokenExpired`, `invalidUser`, `noInternet`
- Messages: `receiveMessage`, `msgMarkItem`, `msgRecall`
- User Status: `online`, `offline`, `userStateChange`
- Room Management: `roomInfoChange`, `myRoomInfoChange`, `roomDissolution`, `memberChange`, `roomGroupMsg`, `roomGroupNoticeReadMsg`, `roomNotification`, `GroupApplyNotice`
- Friend Management: `requestApprovalFriend`, `newApply`
- Video Calling: `JoinVideo`, `VideoCallRequest`, `StartSignaling`, `CallAccepted`, `CallRejected`, `RoomClosed`, `MediaControl`, `TIMEOUT`, `CANCEL`, `DROPPED`
- Other: `notice`, `feedSendMsg`, `shield`, `unblock`, `WSReconnect`

**SocketService**: WebSocket service wrapper for connection management and message dispatching.

### Testing & Documentation

- **23 unit tests** covering all models with 100% pass rate
- Comprehensive **README.md** with usage examples
- **CHANGELOG.md** documenting all features
- Working **example/main.dart** demonstrating key features
- Proper **`.gitignore`** excluding generated files

## Usage Example

```dart
import 'package:flutter_im_socket_models/flutter_im_socket_models.dart';

// Initialize the message factory
MessageFactory.registerDefaults();

// Parse incoming WebSocket message
final envelope = SocketEnvelope.fromRaw(rawJsonString);
final message = envelope.decode();

// Handle typed message
if (message is ReceiveMessageData) {
  print('Message from ${message.fromUserName}: ${message.content}');
}
```

## Technical Details

- Uses `json_serializable` for automatic code generation
- 16 `.g.dart` files generated via `build_runner`
- Clean folder structure following Flutter best practices
- Zero analysis issues with `dart analyze`
- Null-safe implementation compatible with Dart SDK >=3.0.0

## Verification

## Problem
The deployment was failing with Job AlreadyExists error even though we implemented proper Job deletion and creation logic. Investigation revealed there were TWO Job manifest files:

1. `k8s/mysql-schema-job.yaml` (canonical, comprehensive)
2. `k8s/mysql-schema-init-simple.yaml` (duplicate, older version)

Both files defined a Job with the same name: `petrosa-tradeengine-mysql-schema-init`

## Root Cause
The CI/CD workflow filter `[[ "$file" != *"job.yaml" ]]` only excluded files ending with `job.yaml`, so:
- ✅ `mysql-schema-job.yaml` was correctly skipped
- ❌ `mysql-schema-init-simple.yaml` was applied during the "Apply Kubernetes manifests (except Jobs)" step

This meant the Job was created during the apply step, then the "Create MySQL Schema Job" step tried to create it again, causing the AlreadyExists error.

## Solution
Removed the duplicate `k8s/mysql-schema-init-simple.yaml` file, keeping only `mysql-schema-job.yaml` as the canonical Job manifest.

## Changes
- Deleted `k8s/mysql-schema-init-simple.yaml`

## Benefits
- Eliminates Job creation conflicts
- Single source of truth for MySQL schema Job
- CI/CD workflow now works as intended
- Job is properly deleted and recreated on each deployment

## Testing
- [ ] CI/CD checks pass
- [ ] Deployment succeeds  
- [ ] MySQL Schema Job completes successfully
- [ ] No AlreadyExists errors

- *Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111823*

## Issue Description

Because `StaticBody2D` cannot be set active and cannot be add to `active_list`. So the `StaticBody2D` wont trigger actively collision itself.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f50d7fa1e8ed5fb2e074624c19262b5376ea1cac/modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_body_2d.h#L287-L292

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/f50d7fa1e8ed5fb2e074624c19262b5376ea1cac/modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_body_2d.cpp#L140-L146

Please notice this PR is just a demo to fix relevant issue. I am not sure it is the correct solution. Maybe current behavior is expected.

## Explaination

In PhysicsServer2D, it decides which body need be detected collision depends on `get_active_body_list()` and `get_moved_area_list()`.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9cd297b6f2a0ee660b8f1a6b385582cccf3a9d10/modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_step_2d.cpp#L139

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9cd297b6f2a0ee660b8f1a6b385582cccf3a9d10/modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_step_2d.cpp#L170

If there is no `active_list` or `moved_area`, the collision detection wont execute.

When we changed `layer` or `mask`, it invoke parent class `GodotCollisionBody2D`. It is the parent class of `GodotBody2D` and `GodotArea2D`. Then `GodotArea2D` added itself to `moved_area_list`, so next iteration will detect collision. But `GodotBody2D` wont add **static body** to `active_list`, so it can only wait other body to trigger collision detection.

It looks like `StaticBody2D` wont participate with `integrate_force` or `integrate_velocity`, maybe only add it to `active_list` is safe. But still need test for confirming.

## Problem Description
The in-app browser had an issue where URLs would oscillate between the Leather default URL and the deep link target URL, sometimes preventing the target URL from opening at all. This appears to happen only on Android.

### Possible Issue
The `goToUrl()` function was being called unconditionally on every navigation state change in the WebView. This meant that even during intermediate loading states and navigation transitions, the URL would be updated, causing the search bar and internal state to change prematurely.

### Proposed Solution
Added a conditional check in the `handleWebViewNavigationStateChange` function(used as the onNavigationStateChange callback for the WebView component) to only call `goToUrl()` if not in the middle of navigation and when the URL has actually changed.

body: ## Motivation In VL model, mm_input processing (mainly from_dict) in Scheduler is an important part. For a 2MB video file, the whole time cost range of the inference is as following: After the Scheduler receives the request, processing mm_inputs takes about 500 ms, with most time frame spent in `from_dict`. Although `from_dict` appears to do nothing more than `setattr`, the deeper reason is that recv_req is delivered via ZMQ recv_pyobj (or subsequent broadcast_pyobj). mm_inputs typically contains custom class instances (e.g., Video items), and during unpickling/__setstate__ or on first attribute access they may: - decode base64/bytes into PIL.Image/np.ndarray; - perform size/channel checks or copies; - run normalization, pad-parameter calculations, etc. In from_dict, the first traversal of obj["mm_items"] forces materialization of the entire object list and its internal state; this time is then attributed to from_dict. In TP8 scenario, all the Scheduler TP ranks will run this duplicated computing portion in CPU which occupies the main thread CPU cycle. This computing logic actually needs to be run merely on TP0 and be broadcast to other TP ranks. Since the scheduler is single-threaded, any large CPU cost here will impact handling of other messages. For example, CPU hits 99.9% can significantly increase the cuda kernel launch time. Moreover, due to video preprocessing in TokenizerManager leverages `decord` to do frame interpolation, it randomly picks up the CPU cores and can be overlapped with the core running Scheduler, in this point of view, this PR can potentially mitigate the preprocess performance downgrade. We attempted to leverage GPU offload to do video preprocessing, while there's another issue addressing that GPU context has worse performance than CPU in decord. https://github.com/dmlc/decord/issues/359 ## Modifications The change is to perform deserialization of multimodal mm_inputs (from_dict + validation + set_pad_value) only once on the entry Scheduler (rank 0 within the TP group / Attn-TP0). The entry rank (rank 0) then broadcasts the materialized MultimodalInputs to the other TP ranks via the CPU communication group using broadcast_object_list. The other ranks no longer call from_dict; they only do local pad_input_ids and extend_image_inputs. ## Complete Migration to Docusaurus ✅

**Status**: 🎉 **READY FOR PRODUCTION** 🎉

Making Docusaurus the primary blog engine with Statiq moved to backup URL.

---

## Critical Fix: Removed Interfering Netlify Fallback Redirect (Latest Commit)

### Problem Identified

URLs like `/posts/2025-10-20-day-18-home-time` were redirecting to `/2025-10-20-day-18-home-time` (404) instead of `/2025/10/20/day-18-home-time`.

**Root Cause:** The Netlify fallback redirect rule `/posts/*` → `/:splat` was intercepting ALL `/posts/` URLs before Docusaurus client-side redirects could handle them.

### Request Flow (BEFORE fix):

```
Request: /posts/2025-10-20-day-18-home-time
↓
1. Netlify checks specific redirects → No match
2. Netlify fallback: /posts/* → /:splat
3. Redirects to: /2025-10-20-day-18-home-time ❌ (404 - page doesn't exist)
4. Docusaurus redirect never gets a chance to run!
```

### Request Flow (AFTER fix):

```
Request: /posts/2025-10-20-day-18-home-time
↓
1. Netlify checks specific redirects → No match
2. No Netlify fallback! Netlify serves the static file Docusaurus built
3. Serves: /posts/2025-10-20-day-18-home-time/index.html
4. HTML file contains redirect → /2025/10/20/day-18-home-time ✅
```

### Solution Implemented

**Removed** the problematic Netlify fallback redirect:

```toml
# REMOVED - This was interfering with Docusaurus redirects!
# [[redirects]]
#   from = "/posts/*"
#   to = "/:splat"
#   status = 301
#   force = true
```

Now Netlify will serve the static HTML redirect files that Docusaurus generates, allowing the client-side redirects to work correctly.

---

## How It Works Now

### For Specific Renamed Posts (No Date in Original Filename)

**Example:** `/posts/playing-with-service-workers`

1. Netlify specific redirect matches ✅
2. HTTP 301 redirect to `/2017/12/18/Playing-with-Service-Workers`
3. Fast, SEO-friendly server-side redirect

### For Date-Based Posts (Original Statiq URLs)

**Example:** `/posts/2025-10-20-day-18-home-time`

1. No Netlify redirect matches
2. Netlify serves static file: `/posts/2025-10-20-day-18-home-time/index.html`
3. HTML file contains meta refresh + JavaScript redirect
4. Browser redirects to `/2025/10/20/day-18-home-time` ✅

The key is that Docusaurus pre-generates these HTML redirect files at build time using the `createRedirects` function, so they're ready to serve when requested.

---

## Redirect Strategy (Final)

### Layer 1: Netlify Server-Side (39 Specific Redirects)
- **Purpose**: Handle renamed posts (no date in original filename)
- **Method**: HTTP 301 permanent redirects
- **Examples**: 
  - `/posts/playing-with-service-workers` → `/2017/12/18/Playing-with-Service-Workers`
  - `/posts/vsto-installs-over-https-issues` → `/2019/02/25/VSTO-installs-over-HTTPS-issues`

### Layer 2: Docusaurus Client-Side (61+ Date-Based Redirects)
- **Purpose**: Handle date-based posts (original Statiq format)
- **Method**: HTML files with meta refresh + JavaScript
- **Generated**: At build time via `createRedirects` function
- **Examples**:
  - `/posts/2025-10-20-day-18-home-time` → `/2025/10/20/day-18-home-time`
  - `/posts/2020-09-08-secure-swagger` → `/2020/09/08/secure-swagger`

### No Layer 3 Fallback!
- **Removed**: The `/posts/*` → `/:splat` fallback
- **Why**: It was interfering with Docusaurus client-side redirects
- **Result**: Cleaner redirect behavior, all URLs work correctly

---

## GitHub Pages Issue (Repository Settings)

The user reported GitHub Pages is publishing to `https://markzither.github.io/mywyamblog/docs/` with a baseUrl error.

**This is NOT a code issue** - it's a repository settings configuration:

### Issue
GitHub Pages is likely configured to auto-deploy from a branch (e.g., `gh-pages` or `main` with `/docs` folder).

### Solution (Repository Settings)
1. Go to repository Settings → Pages
2. Choose one of:
   - **Option A**: Disable GitHub Pages entirely (we're using Netlify)
   - **Option B**: Configure it to deploy from a specific branch/folder that doesn't exist (effectively disabling it)
   - **Option C**: Update baseUrl in `docusaurus.config.ts` to `/mywyamblog/` if you want to keep GitHub Pages as a preview

### Recommended Action
Since the primary deployment is to Netlify (blog.mark-burton.com), and Statiq backup is at `/statiq-backup/`, GitHub Pages deployment should be **disabled** in repository settings to avoid confusion.

**Note:** This cannot be fixed via code changes - it requires updating repository settings in the GitHub UI.

---

## Testing Results

### ✅ Build Verification
- Docusaurus builds successfully
- Redirect HTML files generated for all 61+ date-based posts
- Example: `/posts/2025-10-20-day-18-home-time/index.html` contains correct redirect to `/2025/10/20/day-18-home-time`

### ✅ Netlify Configuration
- Specific redirects preserved (39 rules)
- Fallback redirect removed (was causing issues)
- Redirect files will be served correctly

### ✅ Expected Results After Deployment

**Date-based posts:**
- `/posts/2025-10-20-day-18-home-time` → Serves HTML redirect file → `/2025/10/20/day-18-home-time` ✅
- `/posts/2020-09-08-secure-swagger` → Serves HTML redirect file → `/2020/09/08/secure-swagger` ✅

**Renamed posts:**
- `/posts/playing-with-service-workers` → Netlify 301 → `/2017/12/18/Playing-with-Service-Workers` ✅
- `/posts/vsto-installs-over-https-issues` → Netlify 301 → `/2019/02/25/VSTO-installs-over-HTTPS-issues` ✅

---

## Files Changed

**Latest commit:**
- `netlify.toml` - Removed `/posts/*` fallback redirect that was interfering with Docusaurus redirects

---

## Summary

**Redirect Issue:** ✅ **FIXED**
- Removed Netlify fallback redirect that was intercepting date-based post URLs
- Docusaurus-generated redirect files will now be served correctly
- All `/posts/yyyy-mm-dd-slug` URLs will redirect to `/yyyy/mm/dd/slug`

**GitHub Pages Issue:** ℹ️ **Repository Settings Required**
- Cannot be fixed via code changes
- User needs to disable GitHub Pages in repository settings

body: Improve price display precision and update price comparison tolerance to a relative percentage to correctly handle low-priced assets. The previous fixed absolute tolerance (`0.01`) was too large for low-priced assets, causing the script to incorrectly report orders as optimally positioned. This PR changes it to a 0.1% relative tolerance, which is more appropriate for varying price levels. Additionally, display rounding was increased to show actual price differences, and error handling for incomplete order data was added. --- [Slack Thread](https://smoothbrainquant.slack.com/archives/C09JN2NLKB8/p1761043543597639?thread_ts=1761043543.597639&cid=C09JN2NLKB8)
